cards.text: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, just went to war alongside Ahab, king of Israel, and Ahab didn't make it home. Jehoshaphat did. He's back in Jerusalem, safe.
He's home, and who goes out to confront him? Jehu son of Hanani the seer, and friend, that man did NOT bring a welcome-home cookie box.

cards.question: Jehu goes out to confront King Jehoshaphat. What does Jehu call him out for?
Because Jehoshaphat helped the wicked and loved those who hate the LORD, Jehu says the ___ of the LORD is upon him.

cards.text: OUCH. The wrath of the LORD. But hold on, baker, Jehu's not done yet, because now he looks at the other side of the king's record.

cards.question: Jehu tells Jehoshaphat that some good is found in him too.
What good does Jehu say Jehoshaphat has done in the land?

answers.text: He fed the hungry in Judah

cards.text: Jehu adds that Jehoshaphat has set his heart on seeking God. That's your boss saying "We need to talk" and then "Also, GREAT work this year" in the same meeting.

cards.question: When Jehoshaphat once again goes out among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, he gathers soldiers for war.

cards.text: Next he appoints judges in each of the fortified cities of Judah. Then he gives them a word: consider carefully what you do.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat reminds the new judges whom they are really judging for. It's the ___.

cards.text: The LORD is with them when they render judgment, he says. And now, may the fear of the LORD be upon them, and they'd better be careful what they do.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat tells the judges to be careful. What reason does he give about the LORD?

answers.text: With the LORD there is no partiality or bribery
The LORD will remove any judge who turns aside
The LORD keeps a record of every judgment

cards.text: Nobody's slipping the judge a cookie box under the table, not even one of mine, and baker, mine are GOOD. Then Jehoshaphat appoints judges in Jerusalem too, to judge on behalf of the LORD and settle disputes.

cards.question: In Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat appoints some of the Levites, ___ and heads of the Israelite families to judge on behalf of the LORD.

cards.text: He charges them to serve faithfully and wholeheartedly in the fear of the LORD. Every dispute from their brothers in the cities, bloodshed or some other violation of the law, comes to THEM, and friend, that's being the one person everybody tags in the group chat when there's an argument.

cards.question: When a dispute comes from their brothers in the cities, Jehoshaphat tells the Jerusalem judges to warn them.
Why does Jehoshaphat want the Jerusalem judges to warn the people who bring disputes?

answers.text: So they won't incur guilt before the LORD
So the courts won't be burdened with cases
So the king won't be troubled by disputes

cards.question: Jehoshaphat names who's over the judges. Amariah the chief priest is over all that pertains to the ___, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, ruler of the house of Judah, is over all that pertains to the ___.

cards.text: The Levites will serve as officers, and Jehoshaphat sends them off with this: "Act resolutely; may the LORD be with the upright!" We'll leave King Jehoshaphat right there for now, friend, but his story is still in the oven.
